text:
tara-support: FYI customer acme-sys opened a ticket — p99 and occasional 429s on their Dedicated eu-west pool since last night. They say it started ~02:15 UTC. Can we triage?

jules-mleng: copying logs now. any quick context on autoscale changes? :eyes:

mike_sre: deploy-bot shows a config push at 02:10 UTC to autoscale policy `dedicated-eu-west-v2` (reduced burst slots). could be related.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: config/service:autoscaler `dedicated-eu-west-v2` updated by ops-ci at 2026-03-07T02:10:44Z. change: "burst_slots: 0 -> 2" -> actually it reduced the burst threshold earlier this week, then bumped back.

tara-support: Customer timeline: 01:50 no issues, 02:20 p95 fine but p99 spiked to 1.2s and some 429s at 02:25, repeated patterns every 10-15m. They provided a few request IDs.

jules-mleng: grabbed tenant placement info. acme-tenant is on node `eu-w2-node-14`, GPU slices: MIG partitions 1g.3gb x6. I'm seeing frequent SM saturation on slice 3 in the same timeframe.

mike_sre: can you paste the nvtop / nvidia-smi log snippet? also kernel dmesg for ECC/fatal?

jules-mleng: paste:```
Timestamp: 2026-03-07T02:24:58Z
GPU 0 (slice 3) SM utilization: 98%
GPU 0 memory utilization: 70%
Process list: tenant_acme (pid 8421) token-gen: 65% SM, other_tenant_x: 28% SM
```

jules-mleng: Also seeing bursts of memcpy and L3 evictions in perf counters.

ada: customer reported auth retries too, any 429 error body?

tara-support: example 429 body from their request:```json
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "compute_queue_full - try again" }
```

rhea-eng: that error usually comes from the autoscaler gating queue when all reserved slots are saturated and fallback denies burst. Could be noisy neighbor on the same host consuming shared SM/PCIe bandwidth.

mike_sre: checking node telemetry around 02:20-02:30, noticing high network TX queues on that host and PCIe utilization spikes likely from another tenant doing large batch uploads.

jules-mleng: interesting: acme's model is small (1.3B) so single-request SM use shouldn't hit 98% normally. suspect co-resident heavy batch job. I see a co-tenant `batchy-inc` scheduled on same node doing heavy token generation windows.

tara-support: customer wants a mitigation and repro steps we can try. Suggested immediate mitigation? :warning:

mike_sre: temporary mitigation options: 1) migrate acme to a different slice on a quieter node (live migrate container slot), 2) pin acme to dedicated slice (no co-residency) until we root cause, 3) increase autoscaler burst slots for their pool to allow more concurrent requests.

jules-mleng: repro steps I recommend for support ops:
1. Collect request ids and trace to serving-host: use `redwood traces get --request <id>` to confirm span where queue reject occurs.
2. Pull node perf counters: `sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses,mem_loads -p <pid>` during spike window.
3. Dump MIG partitioning: `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` and `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` to confirm slice mapping.

jules-mleng: quick diagnostic snippet we used:```bash
# find process on host
ps aux | grep tenant_acme
# sample sm counters (requires perf + root)
perf stat -e gpu__sm__cycles_elapsed -p 8421 -I 1000
```

tara-support: I ran traces for two request ids customer provided — both show `compute_queue_full` around the same host and time.

ada: customer asked if this is a billing/charge issue — they saw retries but were still charged for requests that got 429. any policy?

mike_sre: 429 due to queue rejects shouldn't bill for completed tokens but may bill for accepted allocation. We'll check billing logs for those request ids and advise finance if mis-billed.

rhea-eng: long-term fix: improve isolation between tenants using a) revised MIG packing policy to reduce high-SM workloads co-locating with latency-sensitive slices, b) add per-slice SM cap heuristics in runtime to avoid single-tenant saturations, c) autoscaler signal enrichment to consider per-host SM utilization not just slot counts.

jules-mleng: I also found a node-level packing anomaly: our placement engine allowed a 4x high-burst batch tenant next to several 1g slices; packing score didn't weight memcpy/PCIe traffic. Filed follow-up with eng-platform.

tara-support: customer approved migration to alternate node and wants a postmortem. I'll coordinate migration and keep them updated.

mike_sre: action items:
- rhea-eng: follow up on packing policy PR and add a short-term guard (today) to avoid >70% SM on host when colocating latency tenants.
- jules-mleng: run host perf capture and attach to ticket (include `nvidia-smi topo -m`, perf counters, and traces).
- ada: validate billing for the provided request ids and flag any overcharge.
- tara-support: schedule migration window with customer and confirm warmup/cooldown.

jules-mleng: quick note for repro: if you want to simulate, run a co-resident batch generator targeting the same node with a small model and high concurrency — we reproduced the pattern by starting 6x 1.5B synchronous generators at ~250ms token latency.

tara-support: thanks everyone, I'll update ticket and ping if customer sees recurrence after migration. :thumbsup:

mike_sre: adding link to the node capture in case it helps: https://internal.redwood/captures/eu-w2-node-14/1769001234

rhea-eng: I'll open an ops-runbook PR for noisy neighbor mitigation steps too.
